text:
aaron: Pushed canary for rwd-3b-v2 -> kernel-selection heuristic change (select dense-kernel for seq<=8 instead of <=16). Canary sized 5% traffic. Observability hooks on for token-latency and kv-hitrate. watching dashboards now.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for service=runtime model=rwd-3b-v2 canary=5% by=aaron at=1973001122

meera: saw a small overall P50 bump on the canary routes ~15m after rollout. Not huge but P95 on some routes spiked ~35%. Digging.

luis: linking dashboard: https://grafana.company.local/d/RX7sj/model-compare?orgId=1&var-model=rwd-3b-v2&var-env=canary -- token-level waterfall shows shift in kernel time slice for sequences that used to be handled by sparse kernel now going to dense, per-token compute increased.

olivia: can you paste the token breakdown here? we need a quick decision (continue vs rollback) if tail latency keeps trending up.

aaron: quick dump from perf-bot aggregator (summarized):
```
model=rwd-3b-v2 | route=/chat/completion | baseline (stable): P50=42ms P95=120ms KV_hit=78%
canary (kernel-change): P50=48ms P95=210ms KV_hit=62% 
per-token kernel_time: baseline dense=4.2ms sparse=2.1ms, canary dense=5.1ms sparse=2.4ms
batch_shape distribution: small(1-4)=64% medium(5-16)=30% large(>16)=6%
```

meera: That KV_hit drop from 78% -> 62% explains a lot. I see more cold-KV misses (prefix cache not warming) for the canary. Possibly the kernel switch changed chunking so cached prefixes don't line up.

luis: added a comparison panel I created last week: "model_diff_latency_matrix" — shows token-level delta heatmap between baseline vs canary. Heatmap is mainly red in tokens 8..20 for routes X,Y. Seems like the heuristic boundary at 8 is forcing kernel transitions mid-generation for many samples.

olivia: if kernel boundary flips mid-stream we pay memcpy + kernel swap + kv-reload cost. That aligns with the waterfall showing a ~60ms extra tail for those tokens.

meera: quick config diff I ran:
```
- dense_threshold_tokens = 16
+ dense_threshold_tokens = 8
+ enable_midstream_profiler = true
```
This change reduces dense usage for medium sequences but causes many sequences that were entirely dense to now start as sparse and then switch kernels when more context accumulates.

aaron: noted. Also saw increased batching variance: scheduler is packing shapes differently because kernel selection timing changed. More tiny batches for the dense path. Batching heuristics + kernel flip = bad combo.

perf-bot: perf-alert: route=/chat/completion model=rwd-3b-v2 canary P95 increased >25% relative to baseline at 1973001600

luis: repro/trace snippet from a single request (simplified):
```
recv->schedule(1) -> execute(sparse_kernel) token 1..9 -> kernel_select_trigger -> swap-> execute(dense_kernel) token 10.. -> KV_cache_reload -> latency spike
```

meera: action suggestions: 1) revert dense_threshold to 16 on canary + bump to 0% until we can ensure prefix alignment 2) add a per-route KPI dashboard column for "kernel-flip events per-request" 3) instrument KV prefix-key normalization check so we can assert cache keys are identical across kernel modes.

olivia: agree. also let's add a quick canary-specific panel showing "kv_warmup_curve" (kv_hit_rate over request position) and "batch_shape_entropy" to detect packing regressions. If we get clear signals we can safely try a param tweak instead of full rollback.

aaron: rolling plan: revert config on canary to baseline values in 10m if no improvements. Otherwise immediate rollback. I'll post exact terraform delta.

aaron: terraform snippet to revert:
```hcl
resource "runtime_model_config" "rwd_3b_v2" {
  model = "rwd-3b-v2"
  dense_threshold_tokens = 16
  enable_midstream_profiler = false
}
```

meera: I'll create the ad-hoc grafana panels and add them to the "model-canary-insights" dashboard:
- per_model_token_breakdown (token index -> latency bands)
- kernel_flip_rate (per-route, per-1000 requests)
- kv_warmup_curve (kv hit rate vs request position)
- batch_shape_entropy (0..1, higher = more variable batch shapes)

luis: I'll run a small offline microbench that simulates the kernel flip: synthetic traces show ~55-85ms extra depending on KV size. Will share results in this thread.

perf-bot: perf-check completed: simulated flip cost median=68ms, 95th=120ms for keyset=default at 1973001775

olivia: good. that confirms the hypothesis. Aaron, proceed with rollback unless your rollback window hits conflicts.

aaron: rolling back now to 0% canary and redeploy baseline config. infra-bot will announce.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollback started for service=runtime model=rwd-3b-v2 target=0% by=aaron at=1973001820

meera: after rollback P95 trending back toward baseline within 7 minutes on observed routes. I'll keep monitoring the new panels and open a follow-up RFC for a safer kernel-switch mechanism that does not rekey prefixes mid-stream.

luis: other idea in RFC: make kernel choice deterministic per-request based on initial batch shape + sticky flag, so we avoid mid-request flips. I'll draft a perf-and-safety appendix.

olivia: thanks team. please tag any follow-ups with #perf-regression and assign a follow-up owner. I'll schedule a quick sync tomorrow if needed. :thumbsup:

aaron: assigning follow-up to meera for dashboarding + luis for microbench + luis + meera pair to write RFC. tagging here: @meera @luis

meera: created issue infra/perf#4321 with links to panels and traces. will post links here in morning.

luis: posted microbench artifacts: s3://redwood-temp/perf/microbench/rwd-3b-v2-kernelflip/1973001830

aaron: closing canary thread for now. reopen if any residual regressions show up.
